claim: Policy-separation information predicts held-out relational use better than example count or surface similarity
primary_estimand: held-out policy performance conditional on C_sep/VR versus matched baselines
decisive_artifact: Figure 1 policy information curve plus prospective prediction table
main_rival: more examples, semantic similarity, lexical diversity, task ambiguity
required_controls: matched token budget; answer permutation; shuffled/corrupted demonstrations; selection-blinded holdout
allowed_wording: diagnostic demonstrations provide policy-separation information that predicts held-out use
forbidden_wording: the model is a general Bayesian learner; C_sep is a universal law
promotion_gate: prospective held-out win with independent worlds

claim: Relation readability and native final commitment can dissociate under calibrated prior pressure
primary_estimand: Pr(readout=relation,native answer=prior) in prior-opposed diagnostic cell
main_rival: readout leakage; label mapping; prior defined post hoc; semantic ambiguity
required_controls: disjoint prior calibration; independent readout; explicit oracle; wrong-channel; answer permutation; direct-compound control
allowed_wording: relation remains readable while final commitment follows a competing prior under the tested protocol
forbidden_wording: the model internally knows but refuses; a hidden commitment module exists
promotion_gate: RR pass plus prior-opposed PO/CD above controls

claim: Inferring a partner source policy changes native action on held-out content and improves coordination
primary_estimand: paired policy-swap effect on held-out action/message/coordination
sampling_unit: episode clustered by partner and latent policy
main_rival: surface cue following; partner identity memorization; same-policy replay; reward shortcut
required_controls: new content; new representation; unseen topology; random/no-conflict partner; policy swap; native action scoring
allowed_wording: functional partner adaptation under the tested interaction protocol
forbidden_wording: intrinsic ToM; human-like empathy; a shared neural theory-of-mind module
promotion_gate: policy swap changes native action and improves held-out coordination

claim: LP4FM motivates the new object but is not repeated as Paper B evidence
main_rival: duplicate use of saturation or affine transport
required_controls: separate manifests; provenance links; no reuse of Paper A main results as Paper B confirmation
allowed_wording: LP4FM is a static typed source-arbitration result motivating the next question
forbidden_wording: Paper B replicates or proves LP4FM's mechanism
promotion_gate: Paper B uses new demonstrations/readout/partner swap

claim: A greedy policy-separation selector is a consequence, not the paper's identity
primary_estimand: prospective held-out gain at fixed token budget
required_controls: frozen candidate policies; selection-blinded evaluation; random/similarity/diversity baselines
allowed_wording: policy-separation can guide example selection in the tested setting
forbidden_wording: a new universal active learning algorithm
promotion_gate: selector wins prospectively or remains supplement

claim: Mechanism analyses, if added, remain boundary evidence rather than the central claim
allowed_wording: behavioral dissociation does not imply a localized hidden-state mechanism
forbidden_wording: the mechanism has been identified because a probe or steering vector works
promotion_gate: behavioral result passes before any optional mechanism expansion
